title: Japanese audiences and bands
summary: Lewis praises Japanese appreciation of jazz, their large bands, and their interest in a seven-piece group matching a big band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How did you like it in Japan in general?

I like it, I like it because, uh, the people who appreciate it, appreciate it in general. Uh, it is not that, they didn't know, I guess they know, they know jazz. You know, if they didn't know, they wouldn't listen to. Uh, they knew jazz and there. Uh, some good, good little, good musicians there, I mean. And large bands. Uh, when our boys were in there, they were playing no older tunes. You know, like, uh, uh, uh, San Maria Lanad and some of them. But they were playing. Uh, the music was written out there. It's different. From our old, hundreds of years, appreciate it in the state. But, uh, you had to give them credit. You had to give the larger bands. And the larger bands were not like these musicians in the state yet. They appreciated what the smaller group was doing. Uh, I know, I'm sure they knew that we could produce the same sounds, and get the same effects that they would get with 14, 15 pieces. We would try them all. Uh, uh, but they were, they were very interested to see seven men do, you know, what 15 men was doing. Uh, we used to, we would play with special chorus like, yeah, some of the bands, the leader who conducted the band. Uh, we were drummers there that, uh, I would sit around to, and listen to the drummers. Two days before I was up there, six days from our last trip, which I was sick as I could be. We had 45 minutes.
